title: The Broken Ember Anew
premise: Freya Thackeray, a scribe indentured to the temple of the valley where magic cannot follow, is bound by debt to a life of ink and silence — until a feral child arrives speaking the tongue that existed before kingdoms, carrying a stolen ember of soul-fire. The child is hunted by the court beneath the mountain, which bought the soul of Freya's long-lost brother and will reclaim any escaped fragment at any cost. To save the child, Freya must break her bond, cross into the magical world she was raised to fear, and bargain with the court itself, discovering that her brother's soul is the price demanded. In the end, Freya refuses both surrender and theft: she shatters the contract binding all sold souls, freeing her brother only as a fading memory and giving the child a home in the valley — paying for survival not with blood, but with everything she believed about duty.
about_author: Cyrus Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval debt contracts before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people trapped in systems older and crueler than themselves.

chapters.title: Ink Without Magic
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. We meet Freya copying ledgers in the temple, chafing under her debt-bond, in a valley where magic famously cannot enter. A mud-caked child appears at the scriptorium door, speaking an impossible pre-kingdom tongue — and the temple wards, dormant for centuries, begin to hum. Emotional beat: restless longing cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: The Word Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Using old grammars, Freya deciphers fragments of the child's speech and finds her own family name woven into it — proof her vanished brother sold his soul to the court beneath the mountain. The temple elders demand the child be surrendered. Emotional beat: dread as scholarship becomes personal.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Freya and the child (rendered in strange second-person). The court's emissaries arrive wearing borrowed faces, offering to forgive Freya's debt if she hands over the child. She refuses and flees with the child through the valley's edge, where the world's rules begin to bend. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Crossing the Hollow Line
chapters.summary: The child's POV. Crossing out of the valley, the child experiences magic flooding back, and we learn their true nature: a fragment of a sold soul given flesh. Freya struggles to protect them while her own body rejects the magical air. Emotional beat: tenderness between two exiles from different worlds.

chapters.title: The Road of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the road, they join a caravan of the soul-marked — people who sold pieces of themselves to survive. An old woman teaches Freya that contracts can be read, and reading is a kind of power. Emotional beat: cautious hope; Freya realizes her scribal skills are weapons.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Child's POV. Approaching the mountain, the child's memories of the court surface in nightmares, revealing the price of entry: each traveler must name something they love and leave it behind. Freya names nothing aloud, hiding what she'll sacrifice. Emotional beat: grief anticipated, love hoarded like contraband.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Inside the glittering subterranean court, Freya finds her brother — alive, elegant, and hollowed, serving as the court's chief recorder. He begs her to abandon the child and take his place instead. Emotional beat: heartbreak; rescue complicated by the rescued not wanting saving.

chapters.title: A Contract Written in Ember
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Freya studies the master contract governing all sold souls and discovers a flaw: it requires willing renewal every hundred years, and the centennial is days away. The court, sensing her discovery, accelerates its hunt. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration as the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the renewal ceremony, Freya publicly reads the contract aloud, exposing its cruelty, and offers the one thing the court truly wants — her own unbroken soul, freely given — as leverage to void it. Her brother breaks free long enough to add his signature to hers. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice transformed into negotiation.

chapters.title: Ember, Unbound
chapters.summary: Child's POV closing into Freya's. The contract shatters; souls scatter home or dissolve into light, including her brother's, who fades smiling. Freya returns to the valley with the child, her debt erased but her old life gone, and begins writing a new book — this one in the language before kingdoms. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; survival's price paid, love enduring.
